neighbours.label: the person who is held captive or harmed (imprisoned the king, captured American flyers, detention of the opposition): the victim side of captor vs captive
fire: The rebels seized the palace and locked the queen in a tower.
Soldiers rounded up the village elders and held them for weeks.
The regime has jailed dozens of journalists since the election.
Pirates kidnapped the merchant and demanded a huge ransom.
Guards chained the prisoner to the wall of the cell.
The army detained the student leaders without charge.
Bandits captured the young prince and hid him in the mountains.
The secret police arrested the poet in the middle of the night.
quiet: The rebels visited the palace and greeted the queen in a tower.
Soldiers gathered the village elders and thanked them for weeks of help.
The newspaper has hired dozens of journalists since the election.
Pirates traded with the merchant and paid a huge price.
Guards brought the visitor to the hall of the castle.
The army honoured the student leaders at a ceremony.
Tutors taught the young prince and walked with him in the mountains.
The literary society praised the poet in the middle of the night.

notes: card: peaks on the noun for the imprisoned/captured person (king, Prince, opposition, American flyers, German women); the + pole is the captor side (at the hands of, towering over, Viet Cong). Near misses keep the person noun with a non-coercive verb.
